name: Relay: Workspaces & Previews
subtitle: Results, files and handoffs
promotionalText: Inspect workspace output, open supported running apps and follow the source task—all from Relay's Previews tab on iPhone.
description:
Review the workspace, not just the conversation. Relay connects your iPhone to a linked computer or Relay Hosted machine so you can inspect the work it produces and decide what comes next. The repository checkout and task execution remain on the connected machine; Relay displays the results you open.

OPEN WORKSPACE RESULTS
The Previews tab brings together files and supported local web results reported by recent jobs. See which workspace and task produced an item, open it and return to its source task. Running-app previews require the app's server to remain running on the linked machine.

START IN THE RIGHT PROJECT
Browse the folders available on your linked machine, inspect files and start a task in the right workspace. Work stays associated with its project, conversation and run history.

PICK UP A HANDOFF
Use the companion Relay CLI to hand off supported coding sessions from your Mac. On the phone, review the source repository, computer, changes and conversation excerpt before continuing the task. Handoffs use your GitHub repository and a configured Relay machine. Continuation capabilities depend on the provider and session format.

KEEP DECISIONS WITH YOU
Follow sessions across workspaces. Review supported agent approval requests, see the requested action, and approve or deny it from the phone. Provider capabilities depend on the connected machine and configuration.

CHOOSE WHERE WORK RUNS
Connect hardware you manage, or use a Relay-hosted machine. Relay Hosted is offered through monthly or yearly auto-renewing in-app subscriptions. Both plans provide the same hosted-machine service. AI provider access is separate and is not included in a Relay Hosted subscription.

CONTROL AI DATA SHARING
Before sending work to a selected AI provider, Relay identifies the recipient and requests permission. Work content may include your prompt, conversation history, workspace files, attachments and command output, including personal data contained in that content. You can review the disclosure even while the provider is disconnected.

Relay requires a Relay account. Agent runs require a compatible connected machine and authentication with the selected provider. Supported providers include Codex, Claude Code, Cursor and Kimi, subject to availability on that machine. Work executes on the connected machine, not on iOS.

Subscriptions renew automatically unless canceled at least 24 hours before the current period ends. Payment is charged to your Apple ID. Manage or cancel subscriptions in your App Store account settings.

reviewNotesDraft:
REVIEW ACCESS
Use the account in the existing Sign-in Information fields. This account has operator-provided Relay Hosted access; no purchase is required to inspect its machine. Sign-in reconnects a fresh iPhone to the same hosted machine with a separate device credential. Please allow the initial connection to complete.

WORKSPACE-TO-RESULT WORKFLOW
1. Open Previews. The Launch checklist sample appears under Recent workspace outputs. It is explicitly labeled as a preloaded fictional example, not a record of an AI provider run. The HTML artifact, source files and interactive local page are real and use the normal Relay viewers.
2. Open the HTML artifact. For the working page, use Open live app. Toggle the checklist controls to verify interactivity. The page runs on the linked machine at localhost:4317/lab; Relay creates an expiring task-linked preview, so the phone does not try to contact its own localhost.
3. Use View source job to see the sample's explanation and project context. In Workspaces, open Launch checklist to inspect launch-checklist.html and README.md. No AI account is needed for these inspection steps.
4. To run a new AI task, connect your own supported provider account using Settings > Coding agents, or the connection action in the composer. AI access is separate from Relay Hosted. Provider credentials are not supplied with this sample, and it does not simulate provider authentication or AI execution.
5. Supported Mac session handoff uses the companion Relay CLI and the user's GitHub repository. The sample is not a fabricated handoff or approval request. Sessions shows approval actions only when a supported real run requests one.

Published catalog is a separate configured source with its own certificate requirements. It is not needed for the workspace-results workflow and is not automatically authorized by signing in to a hosted account.

AI DATA SHARING
AI data sharing above the composer reopens the selected provider's disclosure, including while disconnected. It names the recipient and describes prompts, conversation history, workspace files, attachments and command output, including personal information contained in that work. Not Now sends nothing. Allow stores permission; a separate Send starts a task. Relay does not send its account name/email, password, device identifiers or Apple payment/subscription details to the provider as account metadata.

HOSTED SUBSCRIPTIONS AND ACCOUNT CONTROLS
Consumer subscription flow: a hosted sandbox includes a 7-day server trial. When the trial expires, hosted access pauses until the user purchases Relay Hosted Monthly (US$9.99/month) or Relay Hosted Yearly (US$99/year) through StoreKit. Both plans provide the same hosted-machine service; provider access is separate. The paywall supports purchase and Restore Purchases. The supplied reviewer account is intentionally auto-upgraded so App Review can inspect the full hosted workspace without waiting for trial expiry or making a purchase. Restore Purchases is also available in Settings. Account deletion is available in Settings > Account > Delete Account.
reviewReplyDraft:
Hello App Review,

We have addressed the Guideline 4.3(a) feedback with a replacement build and a listing that demonstrates Relay's workspace-to-result workflow.

The first-class Previews tab gathers artifacts and supported running-app output from recent jobs on the linked machine. Each result retains its workspace and source-job context. Open live app creates expiring access to a localhost URL referenced by that specific job, allowing the working output to be inspected inside Relay. View source job returns to its task context, and Workspaces provides native file inspection.

The supplied account can now reconnect from a fresh device without invalidating other devices. Its hosted machine's lifetime handling has also been corrected. The Launch checklist starter project is explicitly labeled as preloaded fictional content, not an AI-generated run; it provides a real HTML artifact, source files and an interactive page through the same normal product paths available to users. New hosted machines include the same starter example. No private AI credentials are needed to inspect it. New AI runs require the user's separate supported provider account, as explained in the app and review notes.

Relay also supports companion-CLI Mac session handoff with repository/source context and continuation where supported, and an approval inbox for real supported agent requests. Work execution and the repository remain on the connected machine. We have preserved the provider-specific AI data-sharing disclosure and permission controls.

The updated screenshots show the actual native app and working preview, and the App Review Information provides verified steps for the supplied account. Published catalog is a separate configured feature and is not required for this workflow.
